name: Christian fascism
summary: Christian fascism blends fascist ultranationalism, authoritarian leadership and violence with the aim of remaking national life on Christian faith and morals, with the state enforcing biblical law. Its adherents typically treat their nation or ethnic group as a chosen people and target Jews and other minorities as enemies of a Christian order. The European cases (the Orthodox Iron Guard, the Catholic Ustase) and US figures such as Gerald L. K. Smith are the examples scholars and Wikipedia cite.
scope: Christofascism / Christian fascism as the defining sources use it: (1) the Romanian Iron Guard (Legion of the Archangel Michael), which Block calls 'Christofascist' and describes as melding fascist ideology with Orthodox Christianity, drawing on Codreanu's texts (a key figure of neo-legionarism, so tied here by title only): For My Legionaries and Nest Leader's Manual; (2) the US strand Dorothee Sölle named 'Christofascism' in 1970 and described in her 1990 essay: chauvinist nationalism, militarism, patriarchal family ideology, hostility to unions and communism wrapped in Christianity; Py later applies the label to Bolsonarism. Other interwar Catholic movements (Ustaše, Arrow Cross) and Catholic authoritarian regimes (clerical fascism) are not tied to this name by the sources found and are left out of scope; the committed answers drawn from them are to be reworked in the answers phase.

notes: The label is applied by outside scholars and commentators, and few movements called themselves Christian fascist. Orthodox, Catholic and US Protestant strands differ on church structure, and a few answers (women's rights, monarchy, economic policy) rest on Codreanu's 1920 creed, which the later Guard did not consistently follow. Over half the answers rest on inference from documented principles. Later pass 2026-11-25: answers that rested on Wikipedia (Iron Guard, Ustase, Gerald L. K. Smith articles) were nulled or re-sourced from Codreanu's For My Legionaries, Block's thesis and Sölle's essay. Themes searched in those: religion, leader, family, race and citizenship, communism, economy (1920 creed), spirit and martyrdom. The Ustase and US strands are outside the scope the sources support. Corpus copy of For My Legionaries (2018) is the same text as s1.
